text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to consolidate in the middle of the 124-125 level on Wednesday after recovering nearly two yen from a recent low of 122.70.
On Tuesday, the June ended at 124.50 after reaching 124.61. Traders said they expected the contract to move between 124.20 and 124.80 on Wednesday.

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) is expected to offer one trillion yen of 2.7 percent 10-year JGBs in the morning, traders said. One dealer said MOF may set a coupon rate at 2.8 percent if it is worried about the results.
"The current recovery of the June may see a ceiling at 125.40. Before reaching to that point, there is a resistance at 125.00," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.

Tuesday's rises in U.S. stocks after the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market (FOMC) meeting left rates unchanged could boost Tokyo stocks on Wednesday, a key factor capping the topside of JGBs, traders said.
But a dealer at another city bank's securities unit said that should the dollar fall below 110 yen in Tokyo, this may boost the June to and above 125.00.
